environment.description: Same Actix-web OAuth service compiled to a custom runtime for AWS Lambda, exposed via Lambda Function URL. The function URL is configured with AuthType: AWS_IAM. The Lambda resource policy does NOT include a principal wildcard or public access statement. The function's execution role has lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl permission scoped only to the function ARN. Callers must present valid SigV4-signed requests with iam:invoke credentials from an identity that has explicit Allow on the function's ARN in their identity policy. The Lambda Function URL endpoint returns HTTP 403 {"Message":"Forbidden"} for any request lacking a valid AWS SigV4 Authorization header with permitted credentials. Additionally, an SCP on the AWS Organization OU denies lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl for any principal outside the trusted account boundary (Condition: aws:PrincipalOrgID != o-myorgid).

config.resource_policy: No public access statement; no wildcard principal
config.network: Lambda VPC not configured - runs in Lambda service VPC
config.iam_boundary: Permission boundary on all roles restricts InvokeFunctionUrl to internal service roles only
config.note: Unauthenticated HTTP requests to the function URL receive 403 before reaching application code
